description:
Open an interactive form to gather enough information for your next useful action. Think of this as dialogue compression: predict likely answers and the consequential follow-up each would invite. Nest that follow-up under the answer; stop where you can act. Use informed defaults as editable proposals, never as evidence the user agreed before Submit. Prefer a compact screen over an exhaustive questionnaire.

Use exact option-as-key branches on select/multi for answer-specific follow-ups: {"select":"Database","id":"db","options":["Postgres","SQLite"],"Postgres":[{"input":"Connection string","id":"conn"}]}. Use reveals for checked or selection-wide follow-ups; use when for cross-element dependencies. Hidden answers read as unset even if they have defaults. Conditions use bare ids, selected(id, value), count(id), any/all, comparisons, && || ! and parentheses. Dependency cycles, including ancestor/descendant references, are rejected.

Widgets: text, markdown, slider (min/max/step/default), check, input (placeholder/default/rows), select, multi, rank (partial priority order), group, page. Give choices concise descriptions (because is an alias) that explain tradeoffs. multi.default accepts an option string or array. For long flows, all top-level elements may be linear pages with Back/Next and one final Submit; page.when can skip a step. There are no page.next edges, conversation nodes, semantic routing, or intermediate submissions.

Keep notes enabled; every select/multi already adds Other (please specify) with free text. Unexpected answers and notes are part of the conversation, not noise. Explicit corrections in notes override conflicting selections; if intent remains ambiguous, clarify only what blocks the next action. Name Submit after the consequence. Use globally unique ASCII identifiers for conditions; avoid status, button, error, _notes, _labels, _route, __proto__, constructor, prototype and generated <id>_other_text collisions. Option values must not collide with their widget’s property names. Validation errors include paths: repair the definition and retry before it is shown.

The initial tool response is awaiting_input: the form is open, not answered. Wait for a user message {"type":"popup_result","formId":"…","submissionId":"…","result":{…}}. The classic result is {"status":"completed","button":"submit","<id>":<value>,"_labels":{…},"_notes":"…"} or {"status":"cancelled"}. Submission is terminal. Treat a repeated submissionId as duplicate delivery; do not repeat the resulting action. Cancellation means stop this question; do not reopen the same form automatically. No backend answer storage is provided.

Read only submitted visible values: absent key means hidden or on an unvisited page; input "" means visible but blank; select null means unchosen; multi/rank [] means no selections; check false means unchecked. Select returns option text, multi/rank return arrays (rank in priority order), slider returns a number. Other adds <id>_other_text. _labels explains returned ids; _notes supplies extra instructions. Resume the original task from the actual answer, including surprises and corrections, without pretending the tool’s opening acknowledgment is a decision.

submit.description: Submission label, default Submit. Use a verb matching the requested consequence.

notes.description: Show optional Add a note, default true. Keep enabled to catch unforeseen answers and corrections.

elements.description: Elements in display order. The widget key carries its label.

id.description: Globally unique ASCII identifier; otherwise derived from label. Reserved: status, button, error, _notes, _labels, _route, __proto__, constructor, prototype. Avoid collisions with generated <id>_other_text fields.

when.description: Visibility over visible values only: bare id tests truthiness; selected(id, value) tests an option; count(id) > N counts selections; any(...)/all(...), &&, ||, !, comparisons and parentheses compose conditions. Negative numbers are allowed. Quote option text containing a closing parenthesis. Hidden values read as unset (false, unselected, count 0). References must exist and dependencies must be acyclic, including ancestor/descendant dependencies.
